functions.name: FM.UpdateRecord
functions.signature: MBS( "FM.UpdateRecord"; FileName; TableName; IDField; IDValue; FieldName...; FieldValue... )
functions.description: Update an existing record in a table in one line. You pass to this function table name (and optional filename). To identify the record you pass the name of the ID field and the value for the record. The ID field must be unique. Then you pass one pair of field name and value for each field you like to like to change in the record. Please note that FM.UpdateRecord and FM.UpdateRecords are nearly identical. Just FM.UpdateRecord provides the check to make sure only one record matches while FM.UpdateRecords allows several records to be updated. So with FM.UpdateRecords you can easily erase a lot of data if you pass wrong ID! With plugin version 7.2 or later, you can specify fields and table via IDs and the plugin will lookup them for you at runtime. Table IDs and table names must be unique across all open files for this to work correctly. With plugin version 8.4 or newer, you can use GetFieldName() function to query field names and the plugin removes the table prefix with :: in the field name before passing it to SQL engine. You can use FM.ExecuteSQL.LastSQL function to see later what SQL was created and run. The SQL functions in FileMaker do not trigger OnWindowsTransaction script trigger. If the record is locked, you get an error like this: [MBS] ERROR:  (301): Record is locked by another user. Your script may then wait and try again later. Does not take part in transactions in FileMaker. Changes are made directly to the database, so you can't revert them later with Revert Transaction script step. Please consider using newer JSON.UpdateRecord and JSON.UpdateRecords functions as they take a variable number of primary keys. This function takes variable number of parameters. Pass as much parameters as needed separated by the semicolon in FileMaker. Please repeat FieldName and FieldValue parameters as often as you need.

parameters.name: FileName
parameters.description: The file name of where the table is inside. Can be empty to look for the table in all files. Using a table in another database file may require you adding the other file as an external data source and adding the external table to your relationship graph to grant access.

parameters.name: TableName
parameters.description: The name of the table to insert record into. Can be ID of table, so we lookup name by ID. Can be result of GetFieldName() function as we remove field name automatically.

parameters.name: IDField
parameters.description: The name of the field which provides an unique ID for each record, so we can identify the field. Can be ROWID for the record ID. Can be ID of field, so we lookup name by ID. Can be result of GetFieldName() function as we remove table name automatically.

parameters.name: IDValue
parameters.description: The value for the ID field to identify the record. Data type of parameter must match the data type of the field.

parameters.name: FieldName...
parameters.description: A field name to set. Can be ID of field, so we lookup name by ID. Can be result of GetFieldName() function as we remove table name automatically.

parameters.name: FieldValue...
parameters.description: A field value to use for setting the field in the parameter before. Data type of parameter must match the data type of the field.

$r
; Value:

("Llama.LoadLibrary"; "/opt/homebrew/lib/libllama.dylib") ]
If [
MBS
("IsError") ]
Show Custom Dialog [ "Failed to load library." ;

Loads the library on macOS:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("Llama.LoadLibrary"; "/opt/homebrew/lib/libllama.dylib") </Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="68" name="If">
    <Restore state="False"/>
    <Calculation> MBS("IsError") </Calculation>
  </Step>
  <Step enable="True" id="87" name="Show Custom Dialog">
    <Title>
      <Calculation> "Failed to load library." </Calculation>
    </Title>
    <Message>
      <Calculation>$r </Calculation>
    </Message>
    <Buttons>
      <Button CommitState="True">
        <Calculation>"OK"</Calculation>
      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False">
        <Calculation>"Cancel"</Calculation>
      </Button>
      <Button CommitState="False"/>
    </Buttons>

functions.name: MessageComposer.CanSendAttachments
functions.description: Checks whether we can send attachments. Returns 1 if the user has set up the device for including attachments in messages. This function can be called before having a composer initialized.

functions.name: MessageComposer.CanSendSubject
functions.description: Checks whether we can send subject. Returns 1 if the user has set up the device for including subjects in messages. This function can be called before having a composer initialized.

functions.name: MessageComposer.CanSendText
functions.description: Checks whether we can send text. Returns 1 if the user has set up the device for sending text only messages. If the return value is 1, the client can set the recipients and body of the message. If the return value is 0, the client may notify the user of the failure, or the client may open an SMS URL via open URL command. This function can be called before having a composer initialized.

functions.name: SmartCard.Available
functions.description: Whether SmartCard API is available. Should always be available on Mac and Windows. Returns 1 if available or 0 if not. On a server it would read the smart card attached the to the server, not any client.

functions.name: SmartCard.BeginTransaction
functions.description: Starts a transaction. The function waits for the completion of all other transactions before it begins. After the transaction starts, all other applications are blocked from accessing the smart card while the transaction is in progress. If a transaction is held on the card for more than five seconds with no operations happening on that card, then the card is reset. Calling any of the Smart Card and Reader Access Functions or Direct Card Access Functions on the card that is transacted results in the timer being reset to continue allowing the transaction to be used. The BeginTransaction function is a smart card and reader access function. For more information about other access functions, see Smart Card and Reader Access Functions.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

functions.name: SmartCard.Cancel
functions.description: Terminates all outstanding actions within a specific resource manager context. The only requests that you can cancel are those that require waiting for external action by the smart card or user. Any such outstanding action requests will terminate with a status indication that the action was canceled. This is especially useful to force outstanding GetStatusChange calls to terminate.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

functions.name: SmartCard.CancelTransaction
functions.description: Cancels current transaction.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

functions.name: SmartCard.Connect
functions.description: Connects to a smartcard. Establishes a connection (using a specific resource manager context) between the calling application and a smart card contained by a specific reader. If no card exists in the specified reader, an error is returned. On success we have a connection to a smart card. You can query SmartCard.GetActiveProtocol

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

parameters.name: Reader
parameters.description: The name of the reader that contains the target card.

parameters.name: ShareMode
parameters.description: A flag that indicates whether other applications may form connections to the card. Can be integer or one of the following texts: Exclusive (1), Shared (2) or Direct (3).

parameters.name: PreferredProtocols
parameters.description: A number with bitmask of acceptable protocols for the connection or just the text name of the value for only one protocol. Pass T0 (1), T1 (2), T15 (8, not on Windows), Any (3), RAW (4).

examples.label: Connect
examples.text_code:

( "SmartCard.Connect";
$Context
;
$Reader
; "Shared"; "any" )
Connect
examples.xml_code:

<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "SmartCard.Connect"; $Context; $Reader; "Shared"; "any" )</Calculation>

<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>If [MBS( "SmartCard.Available" ) = 1]
	#Start a new session
	Set Variable [$SCContext; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.Init" )]
	If [MBS( "SmartCard.Valid"; $SCContext )]
		#Query list of readers and pick first
		Set Variable [$SCReader; Value:GetValue ( MBS( "SmartCard.ListReaders"; $SCContext) ; 1 )]
		If [MBS("IsError") = 0]
			# Connect to card
			Set Variable [$SCConnect; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.Connect"; $SCContext ; $SCReader ; "Shared"; "any")]
			Set Variable [$PRotocol; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.GetActiveProtocol"; $SCContext)]
			If [$SCConnect = "OK"]
				#Run a query
				Set Variable [$Result; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.Transmit"; $SCContext; "0200000008000000"; "00ca018202"; 512 )]
				#Result is 4 bytes. Starts with C901 for Version 5.0 or C903 for Version 5.3
				Show Custom Dialog ["Version"; $result]
				#Disconnect
				Set Variable [$SCDisconnect; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.Disconnect"; $SCContext; "Leave" )]
			Else
				Show Custom Dialog ["Error"; "No card available."]
			End If
		End If
		#End Card Session
		Set Variable [$SCRelease; Value:MBS( "SmartCard.Release" ; $SCContext )]
	Else
		Show Custom Dialog ["Error"; "Failed to initalize"]
	End If
Else
	Show Custom Dialog ["Error"; "No SmartCard API on this OS."]
End If</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>

functions.name: SmartCard.PerformSignature
functions.description: Performs signature. Convenience function which wraps a few calls to Transmit function. With plugin version 7.1 the length of hash is variable. This is function for atos Smartcards CardOS v5.0/5.3, which we needed for point of sales software in Austria. It may not work with your cards unless they have same protocol.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

parameters.name: DeviceType
parameters.description: Which device to handle, so the plugin talks the right dialect. Currently supported cardos and acos.

parameters.name: Hash
parameters.description: The input hash to sign. Length should be 40 hex characters, so it's decoded 20 bytes.

parameters.name: ReturnType
parameters.description: What format to return the certificate. Can be Hex or Base64. Default is hex.

parameters.description: Which device to handle, so the plugin talks the right dialect. Currently supported cardos and acos.

parameters.name: ReturnType

functions.name: SmartCard.Reconnect
functions.description: Reconnects to smart card with different protocol. The Reconnect function reestablishes an existing connection between the calling application and a smart card. This function moves a card handle from direct access to general access, or acknowledges and clears an error condition that is preventing further access to the card. On success we have a connection to a smart card. You can query SmartCard.GetActiveProtocol

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

parameters.name: ShareMode
parameters.description: A flag that indicates whether other applications may form connections to the card. Can be integer or one of the following texts: Exclusive (1), Shared (2) or Direct (3).

parameters.name: PreferredProtocols
parameters.description: A number with bitmask of acceptable protocols for the connection or just the text name of the value for only one protocol. Pass T0 (1), T1 (2), T15 (8, not on Windows), Any (3), RAW (4).

parameters.name: Initialization
parameters.description: Type of initialization that should be performed on the card. Can be Leave, Reset, Unpower or Eject.

functions.name: SmartCard.Release
functions.description: Releases context and all memory needed. Also frees any smart card object.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

functions.name: SmartCard.ReleaseAll
functions.description: Frees all SmartCard objects. Be aware that on a server this may free objects, which are used by other scripts running in parallel!

functions.name: SmartCard.Transmit
functions.description: Sends a service request to the smart card and expects to receive data back from the card. Returns receive buffer hex encoded. see also https://msdn.microsoft.com/en-us/library/windows/desktop/aa379804(v=vs.85).aspx You can use SmartCard.TransmitReceiveHeader to return last Transmit's receive header.

parameters.name: SmartCardContext
parameters.description: The smartcard context reference number.

parameters.name: SendHeader
parameters.description: The hex encoded protocol header structure for the instruction. This buffer is in the format of an SCARD_IO_REQUEST structure, followed by the specific protocol control information (PCI). For the T=0, T=1, and Raw protocols, the PCI structure is constant. The smart card subsystem supplies a global T=0, T=1, or Raw PCI structure, which you can reference by using the symbols T0, T1, and RAW respectively. With version 7.0 or newert this can be empty to use default header.

parameters.name: SendBuffer
parameters.description: The hex encoded data to be sent to the card. For T=0, the data parameters are placed into the address pointed to by pbSendBuffer according to the following structure: Type	name	Description Byte	Cla	The instruction class Byte	Ins	The instruction code Byte	P1	Parameter to the instruction Byte	P2	Parameter to the instruction Byte	P3	Size of I/O transfer The data sent to the card should immediately follow the send buffer. In the special case where no data is sent to the card and no data is expected in return, P3 is not sent.

parameters.name: RecvLength
parameters.description: The number of bytes for the receiving buffer. How many bytes the plugin allocates for the answer. Can be much bigger than what you expect.

functions.name: Time.Format
functions.description: Formats a date with C time formatting functions. locale is the name of the locale to use. You can pass empty string to use default/current locale. Format is a format string like for strftime command in C. The format specification is a string and may contain special character sequences called conversion specifications, each of which is introduced by a '%' character and terminated by some other character known as a conversion specifier character. All other character sequences are ordinary character sequences. The characters of ordinary character sequences (including the null byte) are copied verbatim from format to s. functions.name: Time.Parse
functions.description: Parses a date. The Time.Parse function parses the string in the parameter, according to the string pointed to by format parameter, and returns the result as timestamp.  The resulting values will be relative to the local time zone.  Thus, it can be considered the reverse operation of Time.Format . The Time.Parse function is the converse function to Time.Format and converts the character string pointed to by s to values which are stored in the date, using the format specified by format. Here format is a character string that consists of field descriptors and text characters, reminiscent of scanf (in C++). Each field descriptor consists of a % character followed by another character that specifies the replacement for the field descriptor. All other characters in the format string must have a matching character in the input string, except for whitespace, which matches zero or more whitespace characters in the input string. There should be whitespace or other alphanumeric characters between any two field descriptors. The Time.Parse function processes the input string from left to right. Each of the three possible input elements (whitespace, literal, or format) are handled one after the other. If the input cannot be matched to the format string the function stops. The remainder of the format and input strings are not processed. The supported input field descriptors are listed below. In case a text string (such as a weekday or month name) is to be matched, the comparison is case insensitive. In case a number is to be matched, leading zeros are permitted but not required.

functions.result: the version as an 8 digit number as text.

examples.label: Queries version for auto update:
examples.text_code:
MBS
("VersionAutoUpdate")
Queries version for auto update:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS("VersionAutoUpdate")</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

examples.label: Convert from display format to auto update format:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>Let ( [
v = Substitute ( MBS Update::VersionDisplayText ; "." ; ¶ );
v1 = GetAsNumber ( GetValue ( v ; 1 ) );
v2 = GetAsNumber ( GetValue ( v ; 2 ) );
v3 = GetAsNumber ( GetValue ( v ; 3 ) );
v4 = GetAsNumber ( GetValue ( v ; 4 ) )
 ]; v4+v3*100+v2*10000+v1*1000000)</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

functions.name: WebPolicyDelegate.AddMimeType
functions.description: Adds a mime type to the action list for the policy decisions.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: MIME Type as text.

parameters.name: Action
parameters.description: The action you want to be made. This can be "use" when file should be viewed, "download" if file should be downloaded and "ignore" if file should be ignored.

examples.label: Makes sure all PDF files are downloaded:
examples.text_code:
MBS
( "
WebDownloadDelegate.Install
" ; "web" )
MBS
( "WebPolicyDelegate.AddMimeType"; "application/pdf"; "download" )
Makes sure all PDF files are downloaded:
examples.xml_code:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<fmxmlsnippet type="FMObjectList">
  <Step enable="True" id="141" name="Set Variable">
    <Value>
      <Calculation>MBS( "WebDownloadDelegate.Install" ; "web" )
MBS( "WebPolicyDelegate.AddMimeType"; "application/pdf"; "download" )</Calculation>
    </Value>
    <Repetition>
      <Calculation>1</Calculation>
    </Repetition>
    <Name>$r</Name>
  </Step>
</fmxmlsnippet>

examples.label: Add a type to download:
examples.text_code:

( "WebPolicyDelegate.AddMimeType"; "unknown/exe"; "download" )

functions.name: WebPolicyDelegate.Install
functions.description: Assigns this WebViewer our policy delegate as a filter to the FileMaker built in delegate. When using our WebDownloadDelegate, you may see that it prefers to show a PDF with the build in PDF Viewer rather than downloading it. This set of functions serves to fix on problem: Getting the WebViewer to download files instead of showing them. So you can for example register that PDF files (mime type "application/pdf") are downloaded instead of viewed. All other policy things are forwarded to normal FileMaker policy delegate. And the plugin makes sure you don't install the policy delegate twice. Not supported for WebKit 2.x (FileMaker 16 Mac), but may work with plugin made web viewers (see WebView.Create ).

parameters.name: WebViewerRef
parameters.description: Either the Web Viewer Object Name or the Web Viewer ID as returned by " WebView.FindByName " function.

functions.result: Returns OK on success or error.

examples.label: Makes sure all PDF files are downloaded:
examples.text_code:
MBS
( "
WebDownloadDelegate.Install
" ; "web" )
MBS
( "
WebPolicyDelegate.AddMimeType
"; "application/pdf"; "download" )

functions.name: WebPolicyDelegate.RemoveMimeType
functions.description: Removes a mime type to the action list for the policy decisions. When you remove all types you have the FileMaker default behavior. You can use type parameter "all" to remove all mime types.

parameters.name: Type
parameters.description: MIME Type as text.
